objectives: LO 7.1.1: Calculate return measures — simple, compound, arithmetic/geometric mean, time- vs dollar-weighted, real and after-tax, APR/EAR, HPR, total return
LO 7.2.1: Evaluate risk-adjusted performance with Jensen's alpha, Treynor, Sharpe and the information ratio
LO 7.3.1: Match portfolios to the right index or blended benchmark and know how indices are weighted
LO 7.4.1: Compute current yield, YTM, YTC and taxable equivalent yield
synthesis: Module 6 measured risk (standard deviation, beta, R²); this module turns those into return and risk-adjusted performance numbers, so the R² ≥ 0.70 test decides whether beta-based measures can be trusted. The same IRR and TVM mechanics drive dollar-weighted returns and bond yields, and TEY links bond selection to the client's tax bracket. In client reviews these measures, paired with the right benchmark, are how a planner shows whether a manager or portfolio actually earned its keep.

example.title: Did the manager add value?
example.html:
Portfolio: 11% return, beta 1.2, σ 16%, R² 0.85. Market 9%, risk-free 3%.

  • CAPM required = 3 + 1.2(9 − 3) = 10.2% → alpha +0.80%
  • Treynor = (11 − 3) ÷ 1.2 = 6.67
  • Sharpe = (11 − 3) ÷ 16 = 0.50

R² ≥ 0.70, so all three are usable; positive alpha means the manager beat the return required for the risk taken.

keyNumbers: Beta is reliable → Treynor and Jensen usable; below it, use Sharpe
Bond default: PMT = coupon × $1,000 ÷ 2, N = years × 2, zeros included
Default face value (FV, positive); price is a negative PV
SEC yield measurement window, net of expenses (2026 edition figure)
Textbook annualizes a quarterly IRR by multiplying, not compounding
mustKnow: Real return = (1 + nominal) ÷ (1 + inflation) − 1 — not subtraction
Geometric mean < arithmetic mean unless all returns are equal
Time-weighted = the investment/manager; dollar-weighted = the investor's IRR
Alpha = actual − CAPM required; Treynor ÷ beta; Sharpe ÷ standard deviation
YTC: FV = call price, N = periods to first call
TEY = muni yield ÷ (1 − t); in-state itemizer: ÷ (1 − SMTB)(1 − FMTB)
traps: Using Treynor/Jensen when R² is below 0.70
Forgetting to double the semiannual rate (or using N = years)
Multiplying a muni yield by (1 − t) instead of dividing
Benchmarking a multi-asset portfolio against the S&P 500 alone
Treating a multi-year HPR as an annual return
tips: Discount bond: coupon < CY < YTM < YTC; premium bond: the reverse
In Sharpe/Treynor/IR you can use whole numbers or decimals — just be consistent
Compare Sharpe ratios only within one asset class
